title: Reservation decomposition & autoscale signal contract — Q2 roadmap slice
creator: Lena Cho
description:
Goal: Reduce reserved-capacity waste while preserving latency SLOs by decomposing large reservations into smaller runway slices and defining a precise autoscale signal contract. This ticket captures the Q2 roadmap slice: define signal semantics, implement a light-weight orchestration shim, and run a staged canary across three customers before full rollout.

Scope:
- Design a reservation decomposition model (static slices + elastic overflow) that conserves reserved hours but enables rapid burst capacity.
- Define the autoscale signal contract: meanings, units, TTLs, and required telemetry (queued requests, prefix cache hit rate, GPU util, tail latency percentiles, token throughput).
- Implement a coordinator shim that maps signals to reservation slice actions (prewarm, extend, release) with safety gates.
- Create canary gating criteria, rollout plan, and a production runbook for ops.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive decomposition reduces waste but increases orchestration churn (more transitions). We'll limit transitions per slice and use hysteresis windows.
- Relying on GPU utilization alone is noisy; combine it with request queue pressure and prewarm hit rate to avoid oscillation.
- Conservative defaults for P0 customers; more aggressive for self-service with opt-in.

Deliverables:
1) Signal contract doc (Confluence) with examples and canonical metrics.
2) Coordinator shim PR and RFC for kernel scheduling intersections.
3) Canary runbook + dashboard pre-charts (SLOs & cost delta).
4) Ops playbook for rapid rollback and manual override APIs.

Success metrics (primary):
- Reserved-hour utilization delta: +12% within 30 days of canary for opt-in cohorts.
- 99th percentile latency stays within existing SLOs (no worse than +5ms median change).
- Canary rollbacks required: 0 in staged rollout.

Expectations for teams:
- Infra/Eng: implement coordinator endpoints and metrics exports.
- Runtime: support prewarm extend/release API and tag slices.
- Console: dashboard tile and canary toggle.
- Support/Success: customer communications and opt-in flows.
acceptance_criteria: Signal contract published with examples and unit semantics and reviewed by Infra, Runtime, and Console leads
Coordinator shim merged and feature-flagged in staging with integration tests against runtime prewarm API
Canary runbook written with explicit gating thresholds and rollback steps
Dashboard shows reservation slice health and cost delta for canary customers
No customer-facing incidents caused by canary in first 14 days
updates: 2026-02-10: Initial scope sketched in PM kickoff meeting. Agreed on signal dimensions: queue_length, prewarm_hit_rate, gpu_util_5m, tail_99_latency, token_throughput.
2026-02-22: Infra spike completed — prototype coordinator accepts CSV signals and produces prewarm requests. Found 12% variance in GPU util baseline across machine families.
2026-03-03: Runtime team proposed throttle hysteresis window of 30s to prevent oscillation; accepted after trade-off review.
2026-03-10: Console PO approved dashboard mock; engineering to implement metric exports and a canary toggle feature-flag.
2026-03-14: Finalized acceptance criteria and canary cohorts (3 mid-market customers with predictable diurnal traffic).
risks: Oscillation risk if signal TTLs are too short — mitigated by hysteresis and transition limits
Edge-case spikes could preempt warmups leading to SLO violations — mitigation: conservative prewarm sizing and fallback to dedicated backfill
Billing/analytics mismatch for reserved-hour accounting — requires cross-team reconciliation and small billing patch
Rollout coordination complexity across regions and hardware families could delay canary
metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency for generation endpoints (no regression >5ms median)
Prewarm hit rate: ratio of requests served from prewarm / total requests
Autoscale action rate: transitions per hour (guardrail < 3 per slice/day)
Cost per effective token: compare reserved vs. elastic modes
